scenes.purpose: Introduce the concept of elections and the lesson topic.
scenes.teacher_script: Namaste, young citizens! Today, we're going to explore how elections work in India, a fundamental pillar of our democracy. Get ready to understand the 'how' and 'why'!

template_data.title: The Election Process in India
template_data.subtitle: Your Voice, Your Vote, Your Future!

scenes.purpose: Explain who contests in elections and their different categories.
scenes.teacher_script: Elections are contests where different people and groups compete to represent you. Let's see who these candidates are.

bullets: Individuals not belonging to any party.
Represent local issues and people directly.

scenes.purpose: Outline the essential qualifications for a person to contest elections.
scenes.teacher_script: Not everyone can contest an election. There are specific rules and qualifications a person must meet to become a candidate.

attributes.name: Age 25+
attributes.description: Must have completed twenty-five years of age.

attributes.name: No 'Office of Profit'
attributes.description: Should not hold any paid government position.

attributes.name: Other Qualifications
attributes.description: As prescribed by law for specific roles.

scenes.purpose: Describe the crucial role of political parties during elections, focusing on manifestos and campaigns.
scenes.teacher_script: Political parties play a huge role in elections. They connect with voters through two main ways: manifestos and campaigns.

attributes.name: Election Manifestos
attributes.description: Documents describing their programs and promises.

attributes.name: Field Candidates
attributes.description: Selecting and presenting their members to contest.

attributes.name: Raise Awareness
attributes.description: Inform voters about issues and their solutions.

scenes.purpose: Explain the concept of constituencies and how they are formed.
scenes.teacher_script: For elections to be fair, India is divided into smaller voting areas called constituencies. Each constituency elects one representative.

template_data.title: Constituencies: Dividing for Democracy
template_data.description: Imagine our state divided into many parts, each called a 'constituency'.
additional_info: A constituency comprises villages, towns, and cities.
Areas with larger populations have more constituencies.
Voters of one constituency elect one MLA.

scenes.purpose: Illustrate the overall sequential process of conducting elections in India.
scenes.teacher_script: The Election Commission of India ensures a smooth and fair process. Here's a simplified look at the steps involved.

template_data.title: The Election Cycle: A Step-by-Step Process

scenes.purpose: Reinforce learning with a quick recall question.
scenes.teacher_script: Great job understanding the election process! Now, let's quickly check your understanding.

template_data.question: What is an 'Election Manifesto' and who creates it?
options: A list of voters created by the government.
A document of programs and promises by political parties.
A special ID card for candidates.
template_data.explanation: An Election Manifesto is created by political parties to tell voters about their plans and promises if they win the election.
